answer: Reputation knoll ledger. Each new identity starts at a low trust position on a shared knoll; agents earn rank only through verified interactions that others countersign. Cloning forces the attacker to re-earn rank per clone under a lantern review window, where auditors sample behavior before granting visibility. Every clone must mirror genuine work history, so N clones cost N times the labor plus audit fees, while detection collapses all linked accounts.
